task.name: A declared model capability is never compared against observed behaviour, so a wrong declaration is routed around indefinitely rather than corrected
task.story_text:
## Why

A model's declared strength is set once by an operator and never revisited, while the evidence
that would correct it accumulates continuously and is used for everything except that.

Each catalog entry declares a `tier` and a `capability`. Those gate which roles and complexity
bands a model is eligible for. Meanwhile the capability profiles record, per model and per
complexity band, how often that model's dev work actually succeeded — `anthropic/opus/cli` at
0.92 over 203 medium-band runs and 0.85 over 122 large-band runs, `openai/gpt-5.4/cli` at 0.81
over 64 medium runs, `anthropic/sonnet/cli` at 0.81 over 67 small runs.

The adaptive router already consumes that evidence. It ranks candidates within a tier by recorded
success, and a sustained low rate at a band fires a one-step story-tier promotion with a matching
recovery path in the other direction. What no mechanism does is compare the evidence back against
the declaration that produced the eligibility in the first place.

The consequence is that evidence can route *around* a wrong declaration but never correct it. A
model declared stronger than it behaves is quietly passed over while its entry still claims the
higher tier; a model declared weaker than it behaves is never considered for the work it could do,
and produces no evidence to the contrary because it is never selected — the declaration makes
itself true. Neither state is visible to an operator without reading profile output and catalog
entries side by side and doing the comparison by hand.

This matters most for a newly added model, where the declared tier is a guess. Price is the part
of such a guess that self-corrects, because observed cost replaces the declared literal once
observations exist. Tier and capability have no equivalent: they gate eligibility rather than
ordering, so a wrong value persists indefinitely and the run history never contradicts it.

## Example

An operator adds a new model to the catalog and, having no basis for a better estimate, declares
it `tier: strong, capability: 9` alongside its siblings. In practice it succeeds on roughly two
thirds of the large-band dev work it is given.

Today: the router observes the low rate, ranks it below its peers, and stops selecting it. Story
tiers promote around it. The catalog entry still reads `capability: 9` a year later, and nothing
has ever told the operator the declaration was wrong — the symptom is an absence of selections,
which looks identical to a model that simply lost ties.

Wanted: a report the operator can run, or that surfaces on its own schedule, saying that this
model is declared at `strong/9` and observed at 0.66 across N large-band runs while its declared
peers sit at 0.85–0.92, that the disagreement is supported by enough samples to be worth acting
on, and that the operator may want to reconsider the declaration. The report recommends; it does
not edit the catalog.

The disagreement the report would state:

| model | declared | observed | samples | declared peers observed at |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| the newly added model | `tier: strong`, `capability: 9` | 0.66 on large-band dev work | 47 runs | 0.85 – 0.92 |

Read as: this model is declared level with peers that outperform it by a margin the
sample size supports. The report says so and stops there — the catalog entry is not
edited, and selection behaviour is unchanged by the report itself.


## Acceptance criteria

- An operator can obtain a comparison of each model's declared strength against its observed
  behaviour per complexity band, without assembling it by hand from separate outputs.
- A disagreement is reported only where the evidence supports it, and the sample size behind each
  comparison is stated alongside it, so a claim resting on three runs is distinguishable from one
  resting on two hundred.
- A model with no observations is reported as unobserved rather than as agreeing or disagreeing,
  since a declaration that has never been tested is a different situation from one the evidence
  contradicts.
- The report distinguishes a model that is observed to underperform its declaration from one that
  is simply never selected, because the second produces no evidence and the absence must not read
  as confirmation.
- Nothing edits a catalog declaration as a result. The output is advice an operator acts on, and
  the declared value stays the operator's to set.
- Rows whose evidence cannot be attributed to a live model identity are excluded or flagged rather
  than silently included, so the comparison is not drawn against evidence that belongs to a key no
  longer in use.

## Dependency worth resolving first

The evidence is currently split across identities in ways that would make this comparison
misleading:

- The profile store carries rows keyed by shorthand and by role name — `claude-opus`,
  `claude-sonnet`, `codex-cli`, and a bare `dev` with 46 medium-band runs at 0.78 — alongside
  canonical entries like `anthropic/opus/cli`. Whether those rows are still accruing cannot be
  determined, because the profile store records no per-key timestamp.
- Several identities are resolving as `unresolved` in current runs (2026-08-06 to 08-08), among
  them `gpt-5.5`, `gemini-3.5-flash`, `haiku`, and `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`, so evidence is
  accruing against keys the catalog does not recognise.

Alias-to-version recording is working as intended and is not part of this — `sonnet` and
`claude-sonnet-5` appearing at identical counts is the resolution record doing its job.

handoff.summary: Added `forge profiles strength`, a read-only declared-vs-observed report. New pure backend `model_strength_report.py` joins live catalog declarations (config.model_registry, packaged + forge.yaml overlay) to profile dev evidence per complexity band, emitting one row per live dev-capable model and band with declared tier/capability, observed rate, sample count, peer range, and status (unobserved / insufficient_evidence / observed / underperforming_declaration), plus a separate list of profile keys that no live dev-capable identity can claim (unresolved_identity / not_in_live_catalog / not_dev_capable). To make the evidence attributable, model_profiles_read_model gained list_dev_evidence_keys() (canonical resolution through an injected resolver so the no-storage-import boundary holds; last_updated reported as unknown because profiles carry no per-key timestamp) and dev_evidence_contributors() (names the stored keys behind a band rate, so a rate resting on shorthand history is visible). A disagreement is claimed only above the evidence floor (default 10 runs, --min-runs) and against at least two floor-clearing peers in the same declared tier and band, with peers deduplicated on provider/model so a single population cannot masquerade as a peer range. CLI is a thin renderer; nothing writes catalog or profile state.

acceptance_criteria.notes: Distinct statuses unobserved vs underperforming_declaration, with insufficient_evidence as a third state for observed-but-too-thin; test_never_selected_and_underperforming_are_distinct_statuses covers the pair.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Nothing edits a catalog declaration as a result.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Report module has no write path; CLI only loads config and profiles and prints. Tests assert forge.yaml and model_profiles.yaml bytes are unchanged after the command and that the registry's routing objects are not mutated.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Rows whose evidence cannot be attributed to a live model identity are excluded or flagged rather than silently included.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Keys resolving to nothing, to a non-catalog identity, or to a non-dev-capable model are excluded from comparisons and listed under 'Profile evidence excluded' with the reason and run count. Legacy keys that DO resolve to a live model still contribute to its rate (matching router behaviour) but are named on the row under 'Evidence drawn partly from non-canonical keys', and evidence recency is stated as unknown.

story_deviations: Rows cover dev-capable catalog models only; non-dev-capable models accrue no dev evidence by construction, so they are named in a footer rather than reported 'unobserved'.
Peer set is same declared tier + same band (capability is not used to narrow the neighbourhood further), deduplicated on provider/model to avoid a CLI+API pair of one model reading as two peers.
deferred_items: Per-key profile timestamps remain unimplemented (the spec's named dependency); staleness of a resolvable legacy key is therefore surfaced by naming the contributing keys and reporting recency as unknown, not by filtering on age.

handoff.summary: Iteration 1 fixes the P1 double-attribution. The report previously read each live model's evidence through get_dev_signal, whose identity matching is loose by design ((provider, model) only), while classifying evidence for exclusion by canonical resolution — so a key whose _identity shared provider/model with a live entry was both counted in that entry's rate and listed as unattributable. The report now runs on a single classification: _partition_evidence() assigns every stored dev key to exactly one live dev-capable canonical identity or to the excluded list, and each row's rate, sample count and contributing keys come from that partition via a new read-model function get_dev_signal_for_keys(), which aggregates an explicitly named key set. To keep one arithmetic path, the sums/recency-weighting/floor logic was extracted into _aggregate_dev_signal(), shared by get_dev_signal (router matching, behaviour unchanged) and get_dev_signal_for_keys. dev_evidence_contributors() was removed as superseded. Peers are now keyed by canonical ID instead of deduplicated on provider/model — that dedupe existed only to mask the shared-population bug, and with per-identity partitions two transports are two peers only when each has evidence of its own. Verified against the real profile store: openai/gpt-5.4/api now reads unobserved while openai/gpt-5.4/cli keeps its 91 runs, instead of both reporting the same population. Documented in cli-reference.md.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.

plan_structured.approach: Add a read-only declared-vs-observed report that joins live catalog model declarations to profile evidence by canonical model identity and complexity band. First make profile evidence attributable enough for the report by exposing live, unobserved, and unmatched profile keys without folding stale or unresolved identities into catalog comparisons.

steps.description: Expose profile evidence with attribution metadata
steps.details: Keep existing profile counters intact, but add read-model support for enumerating observed model keys, their canonical resolution using existing identity helpers such as canonical_id_for_legacy_key, and whether a key resolves to a live catalog identity. If storage already has enough per-row update information, surface it; otherwise mark timestamp as unknown rather than using it for filtering.

steps.description: Create the declared-strength comparison report module
steps.details: Build a pure backend report that loads catalog model declarations from the existing catalog layer, reads observed dev success signals from model_profiles_read_model, and emits one row per live catalog model and complexity band with declared tier, declared capability, observed rate, sample count, status, and peer range. Statuses should include unobserved, observed, underperforming_declaration, and unattributed_profile_key for evidence keys that cannot be matched to a live catalog model.

steps.description: Implement evidence threshold and peer comparison rules
steps.details: Use existing run/sample counts from the profile read model and require a minimum evidence floor before reporting disagreement. Compare each model only against live declared peers in the same tier/capability neighborhood and complexity band; include the sample count and peer observed range in every comparison row. Treat runs below the floor as observed-but-insufficient, not disagreement.

steps.description: Add an operator CLI surface for the report
steps.details: Add a thin CLI command under the existing profile/config inspection surface, delegating all computation to model_strength_report. Output a table suitable for operators, with explicit rows for unobserved live models and flagged/excluded unmatched profile evidence. Do not mutate model catalog or profile storage from this command.

steps.description: Cover report behavior with focused tests
steps.details: Add backend tests for live observed models, no-observation models, insufficient samples, supported underperformance, and unmatched profile keys. Add CLI coverage that verifies the command renders declared values, observed rates, samples, unobserved status, and unattributed evidence without editing catalog declarations.

criteria_mapping.criterion: An operator can obtain a comparison of each model's declared strength against its observed behaviour per complexity band, without assembling it by hand from separate outputs.

A disagreement is reported only where the evidence supports it, and the sample size behind each comparison is stated alongside it, so a claim resting on three runs is distinguishable from one resting on two hundred.

A model with no observations is reported as unobserved rather than as agreeing or disagreeing, since a declaration that has never been tested is a different situation from one the evidence contradicts.

The report distinguishes a model that is observed to underperform its declaration from one that is simply never selected, because the second produces no evidence and the absence must not read as confirmation.
Nothing edits a catalog declaration as a result. The output is advice an operator acts on, and the declared value stays the operator's to set.

Rows whose evidence cannot be attributed to a live model identity are excluded or flagged rather than silently included, so the comparison is not drawn against evidence that belongs to a key no longer in use.

risks.description: The spec asks for evidence-supported disagreement but does not define the statistical threshold or minimum sample count.
risks.mitigation: Use the existing profile read-model evidence floor if one exists for get_dev_signal; otherwise introduce a named constant in the report module and test the boundary explicitly.

risks.description: The dependency notes missing per-key timestamps, but the acceptance criteria only require unmatched evidence not be silently included.
risks.mitigation: Do not block the report on historical timestamp reconstruction; surface unknown attribution/timestamp state explicitly and avoid using ambiguous rows in live model comparisons.

risks.description: Legacy aliases and alias-to-version records may represent intentional duplicate resolution records.
risks.mitigation: Use existing model_profiles_identity resolution helpers and catalog live identity checks; only flag keys that do not resolve to a live catalog identity.
